subject: Uzbekistan
note: Hand-curated research for a Geographica episode about doubly landlocked countries. Claims are cited to pinned Wikipedia revisions (trusted_secondary).

claims.text: There are two doubly landlocked countries, surrounded by other landlocked nations: Liechtenstein and Uzbekistan.
Liechtenstein lies between Austria to the east and north-east and Switzerland to the north-west, west and south.
Liechtenstein is the sixth-smallest sovereign state in the world by area.
Uzbekistan is bordered by Kazakhstan to the north, Kyrgyzstan to the northeast, Tajikistan to the southeast, Afghanistan to the south, and Turkmenistan to the south-west.
Due to its location within a series of endorheic basins, none of Uzbekistan’s rivers lead to the sea.
